title: Win32: pipe: Retrieve extension associations when spawning commands
description:
Retrieve the interpreter command for extensions on Windows, and use that
to augment the command line properly before calling CreateProcess
(which doesn't know about them) so that Python, or other language
scripts with associations in the registry, can be executed correctly
without wrapper scripts.

For extcaps, this still requires setting the PATHEXT environment variable,
so that g_file_test reports the file as executable. That guards against
trying to open the program with something like a text editor or IDE by
making things a little more difficult, though someone could still get
themselves into trouble by switching the association (in which case the
file will open up in the text editor when starting Wireshark and loading
the extcaps.)

Skip execution of scripts if a wrapper, identified as a executable of
    the same name but with a .bat, .exe, or .cmd extension, exists in the
    same directory. We probably should have a more general method for extcaps
    with the same interface name, as the interface name appears to be used
    for lookups in the code in a number of places, and name collisions
    probably pose an issue.

Update the documentation in the WSDG and the comments in the example
    Python extcap.

Fix #15710

notes.body: @Lekensteyn, it seems like you started with this approach 7 years earlier and then it didn't get merged. Do you happen to remember why?

It has been a long time, but based on the unfinished two changes, my guess is that I wasn't happy with `.py` files not working out-of-the-box when the Python installer didn't populate `PATHEXT`. If I am not mistaken, this patch has the same issue, requiring `PATHEXT` to be set?

For reference, here is a branch with the two changes referenced in the linked issue:

https://github.com/Lekensteyn/wireshark/compare/bug/15710~2...bug/15710

* Add direct support for running Python extcap programs on Windows https://github.com/Lekensteyn/wireshark/commit/fb3881a6e7d4b54ea94332928fc77987e9c3f725
* extcap: skip execution of scripts if a wrapper exists on Windows https://github.com/Lekensteyn/wireshark/commit/f7d2a15bcd8c94e386d8a3a948386745de3c4973

To support `.py` when PATHEXT is not set, I proposed the second patch above to ignore wrapper scripts. So when `foo.py` and `foo.cmd` are set, assume that the latter is a wrapper for the former. That wasn't very pretty though and required extcap distributors to ship both files.

See also the first patch, the FIXME comment in the test suite is still valid. Once `.py` extcaps are supported, then the test should probably be re-enabled.

I think in general we should do a better job dealing with multiple extcap scripts of all kinds that define the same interface name. There's a check for having exactly the same file in both directories, but I think some other things might break if the names are re-used, with how the names are used for looking up the parameters.

+
+Running a script directly has the advantage of faster startup and only having

commits_data.message:
Win32: pipe: Retrieve extension associations when spawning commands

Retrieve the interpreter command for extensions on Windows, and use that
to augment the command line properly before calling CreateProcess
(which doesn't know about them) so that Python, or other language
scripts with associations in the registry, can be executed correctly
without wrapper scripts.

For extcaps, this still requires setting the PATHEXT environment variable,
so that g_file_test reports the file as executable. That guards against
trying to open the program with something like a text editor or IDE by
making things a little more difficult, though someone could still get
themselves into trouble by switching the association (in which case the
file will open up in the text editor when starting Wireshark and loading
the extcaps.)

Skip execution of scripts if a wrapper, identified as a executable of
the same name but with a .bat, .exe, or .cmd extension, exists in the
same directory. We probably should have a more general method for extcaps
with the same interface name, as the interface name appears to be used
for lookups in the code in a number of places, and name collisions
probably pose an issue.

Update the documentation in the WSDG and the comments in the example
Python extcap.

Fix #15710

Co-authored-by: Peter Wu <peter@lekensteyn.nl>
